question.problem:
$$
V=\text{Span}\{[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1 \\ -1\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ -3 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\},\,B=\{[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1 \\ -1\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}a \\ b \\ c\end{aligned}]\}
$$

Consider the subspace $V$ and an orthogonal basis $B$ of $V,$ given above. Given that $B$ is derived from $V$ using the Gram-Schmidt process, what is the value of $\frac{b}{a}?$
question.worked_solution:
First, let's denote

$\,$ ${a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1 \\ -1\end{aligned}]\,$ and $\,{a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ -3 \\ 1\end{aligned}].$ 

We proceed to find an orthogonal basis using the Gram-Schmidt process, as follows.

**Step 1**: We set ${v}_{1}={a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1 \\ -1\end{aligned}].$

**Step 2**: Next, we find ${v}_{2}$, using the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}{v}_{2} & ={a}_{2}-\frac{{a}_{2}\cdot {v}_{1}}{{v}_{1}\cdot {v}_{1}}{v}_{1}.\end{aligned}
$$

Applying the formula for ${v}_{2}$ in our case gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{v}_{2} & ={a}_{2}-\frac{(-1)\cdot 2+(-3)\cdot 1+1\cdot (-1)}{{2}^{2}+{1}^{2}+(-1)^{2}}{v}_{1} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ -3 \\ 1\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -2 \\ 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $B=\{{v}_{1},{v}_{2}\}=\{[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1 \\ -1\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -2 \\ 0\end{aligned}]\}$ is an orthogonal basis for $V.$

Finally, $a=1,$ $b=-2,$ and  

$$
\frac{b}{a}=\frac{-2}{1}=-2.
$$
